subject: parboot: providing inits and avoiding SE ?

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: parboot: providing inits and avoiding SE ?
parts:
Dear unmarked ones,

I have a rather complex dynamic occupancy model (i.e., with covariates on all params) for which I would like to get a bootstrap GOF assessment using the code in the colext vignette. Getting MLEs takes about 1100 secs, but providing inits and avoiding to compute SEs drastically reduces run time.

Is it possible to specify in parboot inits and the choice SE=FALSE ?

Thanks and kind regards -- Marc

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] parboot: providing inits and avoiding SE ?
parts:
Hi Marc,

parboot automatically sets se=FALSE, and uses the MLEs as the starting values. The code can be seen using the confusing command:

       getMethod("parboot", "unmarkedFit")

Note the key line:

        fits[[i]] <- update(object, data = simdata, starts = ests, se = FALSE)


Let me know if you see room for improvement.

Richard

messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] parboot: providing inits and avoiding SE ?
parts:
hi Richard,

parboot does not allow covariates, right ? I tried that and got NA's for the chisquared test statistic. Then I went back to the data set that we used in the colext vignette and produced a sample of 100 for the fully time-dependent dynamic occupancy model (without covariates). The result is that the model seems to fit much better than it should; see below:

> pb.gof

Call: parboot(object = m0, statistic = chisq, nsim = 100, report = T)

Parametric Bootstrap Statistics:
t0 mean(t0 - t_B) StdDev(t0 - t_B) Pr(t_B > t0)
1 7407 -94.1 12.3 0.99

t_B quantiles:
0% 2.5% 25% 50% 75% 97.5% 100%
t*1 7472 7477 7494 7501 7509 7524 7534

t0 = Original statistic compuated from data
t_B = Vector of bootstrap samples

Any ideas what this could mean ?
Thanks and kind regards -- Marc

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] parboot: providing inits and avoiding SE ?
parts:
Hi Marc,

parboot does allow for covariates. However, if there are missing covariate values, the fit-statistic needs to be written so that they are ignored. It looks like the function we put in the vignette needs to be modified. It should work if you change the last line to:

sum((y-fv)^2/(fv*(1-fv)), na.rm=TRUE)


Regarding your second question, I think the high P-value is just due to chance. I simulated a new dataset and got a P-value close to the expected value of  0.5:

> m1

Call:
colext(psiformula = ~1, gammaformula = ~year - 1, epsilonformula = ~year -
    1, pformula = ~year - 1, data = simUMF, se=FALSE)

>  pb.gof

Call: parboot(object = m1, statistic = chisq, nsim = 50, report = 1)

Parametric Bootstrap Statistics:
    t0 mean(t0 - t_B) StdDev(t0 - t_B) Pr(t_B > t0)
1 7500          0.329             2.64        0.529

t_B quantiles:
      0% 2.5%  25%  50%  75% 97.5% 100%

t0 = Original statistic compuated from data
t_B = Vector of bootstrap samples
Perhaps more testing is in order though.

Richard
